Lord with a Shofar sound'. And it is said: 'with trumpets and the Shofar sound cry out before the King, the Lord'. And it was said: 'And on that day the great Shofar will be blown and the wanderers in the land of Assyria and the banished in the land of Egypt shall come and prostrate themselves to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem'. And it was said: 'And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. ככתוב

As it is written in Thy holy words: Halleluyah, praise God in His sanctuary, praise Him in His strong firmament. Praise Him for His mighty deeds, praise Him for the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the Shofar's blast, praise Him with zither and harp. תחת

Instead of the sons of Zion the sons of Yavan were laid low, Thou didst make Thy arrows flash and confound them with a voice. Thunder against my plunderers, blow with the Shofar, in the whirlwinds of the south let there go forth a voice.

As it is written through Thy prophet: 'And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. The Lord of Hosts will protect them'. So mayest Thou protect Thy people Israel with Thy peace.

אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ תְּקַע בְּשׁוֹפָר גָּדוֹל לְחֵרוּתֵנוּ וְשָׂא נֵס לְקַבֵּץ גָּלֻיּוֹתֵינוּ וְקָרֵב פְּזוּרֵינוּ מִבֵּין הַגּוֹיִם וּנְפוּצוֹתֵינוּ כַּנֵּס מִיַּרְכְּתֵי אָרֶץ וַהֲבִיאֵנוּ לְצִיּוֹן עִירְךָ בְּרִנָּה וְלִירוּשָׁלַ͏ִם בֵּית מִקְדָּשְׁךָ בְּשִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם וְשָׁם נַעֲשֶׂה לְפָנֶיךָ אֶת קָרְבְּנוֹת חוֹבוֹתֵינוּ כְּמִצְוָה (כ״א כִּמְצֻוָּה) עָלֵינוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה עַבְדֶּךָ מִפִּי כְבוֹדֶךָ כָּאָמוּר: וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶם וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֮ וּבְרָאשֵׁי חָדְשֵׁכֶם֒ וּתְקַעְתֶּם בַּחֲצֹצְרֹת עַל עֹלֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַל זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לְזִכָּרוֹן֙ לִפְנֵי אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲנִי יְיָ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם: כִּי אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹל שׁוֹפָר וּמַאֲזִין תְּרוּעָה וְאֵין דּוֹמֶה לָּךְ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ שׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹל תְּרוּעַת עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרַחֲמִים:

blocks.text: 144 Musaph for the New Year 144
א״א

Our God and God of our fathers, blow the great Shofar for our freedom and raise a banner for the gathering of our exiles and bring near our dispersed ones from the corners of the earth and bring us to Zion Thy city in mirth and to Jerusalem Thy sanctuary in eternal joy and there we will perform before Thee our sacrificial obligations according to the commandment given to us in Thy Torah through Thy servant Moses from the mouth of Thy glory as it is said: 'and on the day of your rejoicing and on your festivals and on your new moons, you shall blow trumpets over your whole-offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings and they shall be a reminder on your behalf before your God, I am the Lord your God'. For Thou dost hear the sound of the Shofar and listen to Teruah and there is none like Thee. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who hearest the Teruah sound of His people Israel in compassion.
The Shofar is blown (but not on the Sabbath).
היום

On this day the world was completed. On this day He brings to judgment all the world's creatures, either like children or like slaves. If like children, then have mercy upon us as a father has mercy on children. If like slaves, then our eyes are lifted to Thee until Thou wilt be gracious to us and make our verdict shine forth like light, O Awe-inspiring and Holy One.
uncertainties: 'chil-dren' was a line-wrap hyphen and has been joined to 'children'

blocks.text: ארשת

May the utterance of our lips be pleasing before Thee, O lofty and exalted God, who understands and listens, pays heed and hearkens to the sound of (the memory of) our Tekioth. Mayest Thou accept with compassion and favour the order of our Shofaroth.
רצה

Take delight, O Lord our God, in Thy people Israel and in their prayer and restore the service to the sanctuary of Thy House and accept with love and favour the fire offerings of Israel and their prayer, and may the service of Thy people Israel be a perpetual delight.

blocks.text: 145 Musaph for the New Year 145
While the Kohanim make their way to the דוכן, the congregation say: ותערב
uncertainties: Italic; the Hebrew words are embedded in the instruction

blocks.text: ותערב

May our entreaty be pleasing to Thee like the whole-offering and the sacrifice. O Merciful One, restore Thy presence to Zion in Thy great mercies and the order of worship to Jerusalem. Let our eyes behold Thy return to Zion in compassion and let us serve Thee there in awe as in olden times and former years.
uncertainties: 'whole-offering' is broken across a line at its real hyphen, so the hyphen stays. 'pres-ence' was a line-wrap hyphen and has been joined

blocks.text: ברוך
Blessed art Thou, O Lord, whom alone we wish to worship in awe.
מודים

We thank Thee for Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers for ever and ever. The Rock of our life, the Shield of our salvation art Thou from generation to generation. We thank Thee and tell of Thy fame for our life that is delivered in Thy hand for our souls that are entrusted to Thee and for Thy miracles that are daily with us and for Thy wonders and benefits at all times, evening, morning and noon. O Thou who art good for Thy mercies never end, O Thou who showest mercy for Thy sindnesses never cease, ever have we trusted in Thee.
uncertainties: The source prints 'sindnesses' (presumably a misprint for 'kindnesses'), and I kept it as printed

blocks.text: Congregation:
uncertainties: Italic label over the right column

blocks.text: מודים

We thank Thee because Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers, the God of all flesh, our Creator, the Creator of the beginning. Blessings and thanks to Thy Great and Holy Name for having kept us alive and let us survive. So mayest Thou further keep us alive and let us survive and gather our exiles to the court-yards of Thy Sanctuary in order to observe Thy statutes and do Thy will and serve Thee whole-heartedly; wherefore we thank Thee. Blessed be God to whom thanks are due.
uncertainties: The line-wrap hyphens in 'Cre-ator', 'may-est' and 'Bless-ed' have been joined. I kept 'court-yards' and 'whole-heartedly' as printed, but whether those hyphens are real or just line wraps is unclear

blocks.text: ועל
For all of them may Thy Name, O our King, be continually blessed and exalted for ever and ever.
וכתוב
And inscribe for a good life all the children of Thy Covenant.
וכל

And all the living thank Thee, Selah, and praise Thy Name in truth, O God of our salvation and of our aid, Selah! Blessed art Thou, O Lord, All-benevolent, whose name is goodness and unto whom it is becoming to give thanks.
אלהינו

Our God and God of our fathers, bless us with the threefold blessing that is written in the Torah through Moses Thy servant and was uttered by the mouth of Aaron and his sons the priests, Thy holy people, as it is said:

notes: I identified these sources only after the literal reading. None of the pages prints a citation label. Weekday s306: end of Exod 19:18; Ps 47:6; Ps 98:6; Ps 81:4–5; Ps 150; Isa 18:3; Isa 27:13; Zech 9:14–15. Shabbat s306: Ps 150 and Zech 9:14–15. s308: Num 10:10. All of these verse words are recited text.

I kept the weekday (above the rule) and Shabbat (below the rule) sections apart on s306 and s307, and did not interleave them. The Shabbat poem stanzas are 'בִּנְעִימוֹת קוֹל' (continued) and 'תַּחַת בְּנֵי צִיּוֹן', each followed by its verse.
Fine cantillation and meteg detail could not be fully confirmed at this resolution. Where marks were unclear I left them out instead of filling them in from standard texts.
The Hebrew-script German instructions are on s306 (אַם שַׁבָּת.), s308 (אַם שבת.) and s310 (the Duchan instruction).
